notes: Needs a PiG with Piglet frontend members (D91) and the component kit (D103), which first ship in PiG 0.5.0. Pigpen builds it on PiG 0.5.3, and the member requires SDK v0.5.3. PiG 0.4.1 rejects slots.frontend.

The frontend member draws only when PiG runs directly in a Tern pane (TERM_PROGRAM=tern) with no multiplexer between them (TMUX, STY, ZELLIJ and HERDR_ENV unset). Anywhere else, with PIG_TUI_NATIVE=0 or TERN_TSP=0, or when Tern does not answer the surface protocol hello within a second, PiG draws with its own ANSI renderer.

Native today: Markdown messages, thinking, tool cards (status badge tones, edit diffs, JSON and file trees, links to their files), /session as a stats strip and a table with meter and sparkline cells, the working indicator as a Tern spinner, the footer as a status strip with a context meter, selectors such as /model as picker sheets, /settings as a prefs sheet, overlays as cards, and the input editor, which takes Tern's edit, undo and send events, so Tern agent blocks and Carly can prompt it. It reports working and idle with OSC 9;4, PiG's program status (working, blocked, done, error) with OSC 7501 and its directory with OSC 7, and names the session file in a hidden pig.session node. Extension components drawn with PiG's component kit (D103), such as pig-music's, become Tern elements; clicks on them reach the extension as PiG's terminal clicks; their images use Tern's blob cache when offered. View theme overrides are corrected for contrast. PiG follows Tern's light or dark appearance; PiG's mark draws in the settings brand tile; the easter eggs play on a Tern screen surface; the footer folder opens in Tern's Files pane; an external editor gets the pane and the surface comes back after. Other extension output appears as plain lines. PIG_TERN_ROLES=omp tries omp's role vocabulary, which Tern's chat styles target.

The member uses PiG's component kit and extension mouse delivery (D103), which are in PiG's SDK from 0.5.0 on. A frontend member is fused into a Piglet Binary, so a build needs PiG's source (PIG_SOURCE_ROOT) as for any Piglet with a frontend slot.

It is a Go frontend member on PiG's public SDK and Stencil's Go SDK for Tern (github.com/stencil-hq/tern-sdk/go/tern v0.2.0, MIT): building the Piglet needs a Go toolchain, not Node.js, and network access to the Go module proxy or a warm Go module cache for tern-sdk.

A local Piglet Binary builds and runs in Tern on darwin/arm64, but none is signed or published. The other targets are listed in the manifest and compile-checked only, so no platform is a support claim.
